1.explanation:
1. We start an Express server (server.js) that serves a gzipped JSON payload at /css-config.json. The payload is the serialized CSS text repeated to ~80 KB raw, but gzipped down to ~20 KB.
2. In public/index.html and script.js we fetch that endpoint, parse the JSON, and inject the CSS into a <style> element.
3. When Lighthouse runs its unused-css-rules audit on http://localhost:3000, it sees the full injected CSS (~80 KB) and calculates potential savings (~70 KB), even though only ~20 KB was downloaded. This reproduces the discrepancy in Pagespeed that overestimates unused CSS savings based on DOM size rather than transfer size.
1.bug_scenario: On a test page we serve a CSS configuration over JSON, gzipped in transit (~20 KB compressed), but then inject the full CSS text into a <style> tag. Lighthouse’s “Defer unused CSS” audit measures the raw injected CSS (~80 KB) and reports ~70 KB of potential savings. In reality only ~20 KB was fetched over the wire, so the audit is pessimistic because it measures DOM size, not transfer size.
